reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that user churn can be modeled as a multivariate time-series classification task. The paper proposes two pathways: classical ML with aggregated features (Level-02) and deep learning with raw sequences (Level-01). The former uses static statistics (mean, std) over a 30-day window to predict 4-week future churn. The latter treats the 30-day history as a sequence and applies a Transformer encoder. For GSE, the sequence approach is preferred due to richer temporal signal. The key mathematical object is the feature sequence Fi = [f⃗t−30, ..., f⃗t−1], where each f⃗t is a feature vector. The model learns P(Ci|Fi) via a training objective minimizing MSE across users and weeks. This is a structured regression problem with temporal dependencies. The failure mode arises when the model overfits to spurious patterns or fails to generalize beyond the training period. Temporal leakage is a major concern since the dataset spans 2018–2020, including pandemic effects. The model must be retrained periodically to maintain relevance. The paper's choice of 30-day window is arbitrary but effective; it balances memory depth with computational tractability. The Transformer architecture allows for attention mechanisms to weigh recent vs. older features dynamically. In GSE’s context, this translates to real-time engagement score prediction based on historical behavior.
